uncertain_edges.reason: TR-CPT-A is labelled 480/120 VAC, so a secondary-to-120 VAC relation is plausible, but the visible lower lead ends at a standalone dot left of BUS-120AC-A with no solid joining conductor.
RELAY-27A is labelled UV BUS A and likely monitors the 120 VAC A bus, but only dashed control routing is visible near the relay; no solid bus tap is clearly drawn.
Dashed control loop encloses/approaches RELAY-27A and RPS-PNL-A, but it may represent routed control cable boundary rather than a definite terminal-to-terminal conductor.
B-side dashed control loop visually runs from the relay area around RPS-PNL-B, but the dashed line is treated as routing unless a terminal connection is explicit.
Lockout relay 86A is near the A-side RPS/control dashed loop, but no solid conductor from the relay box to RPS-PNL-A is visually definite.
Lockout relay 86B is near the B-side RPS/control dashed loop, but no solid conductor from the relay box to RPS-PNL-B is visually definite.
A dotted station-ground path appears near the left dashed cable routes and ground symbol, but it is not asserted as electrical bus connectivity.

The 2A-C22 dashed route passes through the ESF diesel A/dashed enclosure area, but dashed routing is not enough to assert an electrical edge.
The 2A-C86 label and lockout relay numbering are plausibly related, but the dashed routing is not a solid, terminal-level conductor.
The 2B-C22 dashed route passes through the ESF diesel B/dashed enclosure area, but dashed routing is not enough to assert an electrical edge.
The 2B-C86 label and lockout relay numbering are plausibly related, but the dashed routing is not a solid, terminal-level conductor.
The reserved 480 V tie label sits between BUS-480A and BUS-480B, but the note explicitly says no connection shown.

notes: Raw schematic was treated as authoritative; overlay boxes were used only as visual aids.
CB-105 is drawn as the 4.16 kV bus tie and the status table lists it OPEN; asserted edges represent visible physical terminals to the breaker, not a direct BUS_4160A-to-BUS_4160B short.
MCC load bucket/local disconnect squares are represented as logical nodes between each MCC and its load to preserve the visually labelled feeder geometry.
Dashed control-cable route/enclosure lines are not asserted as electrical connectivity unless a visible device/contact/tap is present.
The 480 V tie reserved space between BUS-480A and BUS-480B is explicitly marked NO CONNECTION SHOWN and is left isolated.
